name: Nebuzar-adan
description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: In the fifth month of the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard came to Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carries away captive to Babylon the remnant of the people that remained in the city, those who fell away to him, and the rest, but leaves the poor of the people who had nothing in the land of Judah and gives them vineyards and fields.

The word came to Jeremiah after Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard let him go from Ramah, where he had been bound in chains among all the captives of Jerusalem and Judah being carried away to Babylon; Jeremiah was let go when Jerusalem was seized.

note.label: Jeremiah 40: Jeremiah Set Free and Gedaliah Made Governor

points: Ishmael carried away captive all the residue of the people at Mizpah, including the king's daughters, whom Nebuzaradan had committed to Gedaliah, and departed toward the Ammonites.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: Johanan and all the captains took the whole remnant of Judah, the men, women, children, and the king's daughters that Nebuzaradan had left with Gedaliah, along with Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch.

note.label: Jeremiah 43: The Proud Men Reject the Word and Flee to Egypt

points: Nebuzaradan carried away captive certain of the poor of the people, the residue in the city, and those that had fallen to the king of Babylon, but left certain of the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen.

note.label: Jeremiah 52: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Puppet King Zedekiah

points: These are the numbers Nebuchadnezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year 3,023 Jews, in the eighteenth year 832 persons from Jerusalem, and in the twenty-third year Nebuzaradan carried away 745 persons, four thousand and six hundred in all.
